Will Patrick Mahomes play against the Atlanta Falcons?

Kansas City Chiefs fans can finally breathe a little easier after Patrick Mahomes' frightening elbow injury against the New York Jets. The quarterback has received encouraging news following an MRI, but his availability for the upcoming game against the Atlanta Falcons remains uncertain. Mahomes suffered the injury during Sunday's matchup against the Jets on November 8. The Chiefs quarterback took an awkward hit from rookie defensive end David Bailey while attempting a pass, causing his right elbow to bend backward in an uncomfortable position.The moment immediately raised concerns as Mahomes briefly left the field with his arm hanging by his side. However, he managed to return to the game and helped Kansas City secure a 35-12 victory. Now, head coach Andy Reid has provided an encouraging update on his quarterback's condition.Speaking to reporters on Monday, Reid revealed that Mahomes' MRI results were more positive than negative.Reid said.The Chiefs coach also confirmed that Mahomes is currently considered day-to-day as the team monitors his recovery. Reid explained that the quarterback would need some rehabilitation to help reduce the soreness in his elbow.While the initial results have offered some relief, the team is not rushing to make a decision about his playing status. The encouraging news is particularly important for Kansas City, which is approaching a crucial stretch of the NFL season.The initial concern surrounding Mahomes was the possibility of a more serious elbow injury after the awkward hit. However, the MRI reportedly showed no significant structural damage, with the injury being described as an elbow strain or sprain.That is a major relief for the Chiefs, considering how important Mahomes is to their offense. The quarterback also showed his toughness by returning to Sunday's game despite the discomfort. He finished the contest with 23 completions on 31 attempts for 242 passing yards and two touchdowns. Although the Chiefs managed to get the win, the biggest talking point afterward was naturally Mahomes' health.The biggest question now is whether Mahomes will be ready for Kansas City's Week 10 matchup against the Atlanta Falcons on Sunday, November 15. Reid has not guaranteed that his quarterback will be available, and the Chiefs are expected to monitor his recovery throughout the week.The first official injury report is expected on Wednesday, which should provide a better indication of whether Mahomes can participate in practice. If he is unable to practice fully, backup quarterback Justin Fields could be asked to take on additional preparation.For now, Kansas City has reason to be optimistic after receiving positive MRI news. However, the Chiefs will need to be careful with their franchise quarterback rather than risk making his injury worse. Mahomes avoiding significant structural damage is certainly encouraging, but fans will have to wait for another update before knowing whether he will take the field against Atlanta.
Article Summary: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes suffered an elbow injury against the New York Jets on November 8. Head coach Andy Reid revealed that Mahomes' MRI results were more positive than negative. The MRI reportedly showed no significant structural damage, with the injury being described as an elbow strain or sprain. Mahomes is currently considered day-to-day as the team monitors his recovery.

Article Title: "Serious health problems....": Travis Kelce's mom Donna Kelce took drastic action at Florida home after an alarming discovery
Article Text:
Travis Kelce and Donna Kelce (Image via Getty Images)

Why Donna Kelce decided to replace her windows

New Heights

When should homeowners replace their windows?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Earlier this year, Donna Kelce found herself at the centre of an unexpected home renovation conversation. The mother of NFL stars Travis and Jason Kelce decided to replace nine windows and six doors at her Florida property. While the project may sound like a routine household upgrade, her reason for doing so could strike a chord with homeowners dealing with rising energy bills, uncomfortable indoor temperatures and persistent moisture around their windows. Her decision also raises an important question: when does an ageing window become more than just an eyesore?Travis Kelce's mom Donna Kelce's decision came down to two practical concerns: controlling household expenses and dealing with condensation. Florida's humid climate can put considerable pressure on home interiors, particularly when older windows fail to provide proper insulation.Speaking on thepodcast, she explained the reason behind the renovation, saying, “I’m doing something so that I can save money on heating and air conditioning and to keep my windows from sweating,” she added, “That’s as simple as it is.”The project was expected to take three days. However, the problem she described is not limited to Florida homes.Condensation, often called window sweating, occurs when moisture collects on glass surfaces. According to HVAC expert Richie Drew, this can point to excess indoor humidity and poor ventilation. He also warned that leaving moisture problems unresolved could encourage mould and bacteria to develop.“When windows are kept closed, and there’s insufficient air circulation inside, condensation can quickly form on the glass panes. If left unaddressed, this moisture can create serious problems for your health and home as mold, bacteria, and other toxins start to build up,” Drew explained.Donna Kelce's renovation also highlights when homeowners should consider making similar improvements. However, replacing every window is not always the right answer.Drew recommends arranging a professional energy audit before spending money on new windows or doors. An assessment can identify air leaks, insulation problems and inefficient heating or cooling systems. This helps homeowners understand where their energy is going and whether their windows are actually responsible.Older single-pane windows, metal frames and poorly sealed sliding windows can allow indoor air to escape. Replacing them with double- or triple-pane models featuring Low-E coatings can improve insulation and reduce energy waste.For those not ready for a major renovation, smaller improvements can also make a difference. Weatherstripping, window film, storm windows and insulated curtains can help limit drafts. Regular HVAC servicing is equally important, with Drew recommending professional maintenance twice a year.Ultimately, Donna Kelce's renovation offers a useful reminder: windows do more than brighten a room. They also influence indoor comfort, moisture levels and household expenses. Before investing in replacements, homeowners should identify the actual problem and choose an upgrade that addresses it.
Article Summary: Donna Kelce decided to replace nine windows and six doors at her Florida home. Her reason for doing so could strike a chord with homeowners dealing with rising energy bills, uncomfortable indoor temperatures and persistent moisture around their windows. HVAC expert Richie Drew recommends arranging a professional energy audit before spending money on new windows.

Article Title: Tom Brady helped raise $450,000 for human trafficking survivors as NFL legend delivers powerful message of hope and support
Article Text:
Tom Brady (Getty Images)

Tom Brady joins $450,000 Covenant House fundraiser

Tom Brady highlights importance of supporting homeless youth

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tom Brady has spent years making headlines for his achievements on the football field, but his latest appearance brought attention to a cause far removed from the NFL. The seven-time Super Bowl champion joined a major charity fundraiser in New Jersey, helping an organisation dedicated to supporting homeless young people and human trafficking survivors. The event raised more than $450,000, bringing together hundreds of insurance industry leaders. Brady also used the occasion to deliver a heartfelt message about the importance of standing behind young people when they need support the most.Tom Brady attended Covenant House New Jersey's fundraising event on September 23, 2026, where he took part in a 30-minute conversation with Eric Andersen, president and CEO of AIG. More than 300 insurance industry leaders and professionals attended the gathering, which generated over $450,000 for the organisation.The fundraiser focused on helping young people facing homelessness and survivors of human trafficking. Covenant House New Jersey provides emergency shelter, food, healthcare, education and longer-term housing support. Its programmes also help young people find employment and build independent lives.Brady's appearance brought added attention to the organisation's work, but his message carried a purpose beyond the fundraising total. The former New England Patriots quarterback encouraged attendees to keep supporting vulnerable young people and give them opportunities to build a better future.“Thanks for believing in these young people. Thanks for investing in their future. Keep showing up. Keep believing. That’s how we change lives together.”The event also highlighted the insurance industry's continuing relationship with Covenant House. The sector has supported the organisation through fundraising initiatives for several years. Its September 2024 fundraising dinner, for instance, collected approximately $250,000.The latest fundraiser comes as Covenant House continues to expand its work with vulnerable young people. Its FY2025 impact report revealed that the organisation reached 2,373 young people and provided 95,735 nights of housing. It also served 227 survivors through its human trafficking victim services programme.These figures offer a closer look at why contributions from corporate leaders and public figures matter. Financial support helps the organisation maintain shelters, provide essential services and give young people access to education and employment opportunities.Brady has also maintained a long association with charitable causes throughout his NFL career. His work with Best Buddies International, food banks and disaster relief initiatives has included fundraising appearances and direct contributions.However, his participation in the New Jersey event should not be confused with a personal $450,000 donation. The amount represents the collective funds raised through the fundraiser.For Brady, the appearance offered another opportunity to use his public platform to support a cause affecting young people. His message was simple: lasting change begins when people continue to show up for those who need help.
Article Summary: Tom Brady attended Covenant House New Jersey's fundraising event. The event raised more than $450,000, bringing together insurance industry leaders. Brady used the occasion to deliver a heartfelt message about the importance of standing behind young people when they need support the most.

Article Title: India vs New Zealand: No play in Hamilton! Rain washes out third ODI, India remain 2-0 up
Article Text:
BCCI Photo

Rain washes out third ODI after toss

India take unassailable 2-0 lead

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Shubman Gill's last ODI, Shreyas Iyer to lead India

NEW DELHI: Rain played spoilsport once again as the third ODI between India and New Zealand was called off at Seddon Park in Hamilton on Tuesday. Despite a delay of more than two hours, the weather did not allow any play. The umpires eventually decided to abandon the match after rain returned and made conditions unsuitable for cricket.India continue to lead the five-match series 2-0.The two teams will now travel to Mount Maunganui for the final two ODIs, scheduled to be played on November 13 and 15.India captain Shubman Gill won the toss for the third consecutive time in the ODI series and elected to bowl. The toss was originally scheduled for 2:30 PM local time (7:00 AM IST) but was delayed by more than two hours due to rain and a wet outfield. The match was later reduced to 40 overs per side.However, just as the ground staff were removing the covers to prepare for the match, rain returned and forced them to cover the pitch again.There was still enough time to play a 20-over match, but the weather showed no signs of improving. With the local cut-off time of 7:50 PM (12:20 PM) approaching, the umpires decided to call off the match.The forecast had already predicted a 90 per cent chance of rain throughout the day.India had won the first two matches of the series, both of which were affected by rain. The visitors won the opening ODI in Auckland by five wickets while chasing a revised target under the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method.In the second ODI in Wellington, India registered a four-run victory under the DLS method to take a 2-0 lead.With the third match ending without a result, India cannot lose the series. New Zealand will now have to win the remaining two matches to draw the series.The washout also ended New Zealand's run of 11 consecutive bilateral ODI series victories at home. South Africa hold the record with 17 successive home ODI series wins between 2002 and 2007.The third ODI was also the final match of the series for Shubman Gill and senior wicketkeeper-batter KL Rahul. Both players will now join India's Test squad in Wellington. Kuldeep Yadav, Anshul Kamboj and Mohammed Siraj will also link up with the Test team.Shreyas Iyer will take charge of India for the remaining two ODIs in Gill's absence.The fourth and fifth ODIs will be played at Mount Maunganui on November 13 and 15 respectively.
Article Summary: Third ODI between India and New Zealand called off at Seddon Park in Hamilton. India continue to lead the five-match series 2-0. The fourth and fifth ODI will be played at Mount Maunganui on November 13 and 15.

Article Title: LeBron James gets a special shoutout from Bronny’s close friend Tyrese Maxey as Sixers star highlights his underrated skill
Article Text:
LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey. Image via: Emilee Chinn / Getty Images

What did Tyrese Maxey say about LeBron James’ passing?

How Maxey helped bring James to Philadelphia

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Tyrese Maxey was ready to go up for a rebound on what he thought was a LeBron James layup. The ball came to him instead. The Philadelphia 76ers guard laughed about it after the game, then praised a part of James’ game that rarely gets top billing. Maxey, a 26-year-old All-NBA guard, is still learning how his new teammate thinks. James joined the Sixers this summer after deciding not to return to the Lakers, and the lessons are arriving one pass at a time. Philadelphia plays the Boston Celtics on Tuesday.Maxey said he did not think James had seen him. He figured the four-time MVP was about to shoot, so his hands went up for the miss. The ball came anyway. Hands up, he said afterward, is the right habit with James on the floor, because nobody knows when a pass is coming. “You got to become a wide receiver or a catcher at that point,” Maxey said. He laughed through the whole explanation.Passing has always been a big part of James’ game, and teammates like Maxey are only now seeing it from the inside. James reads the floor a play or two ahead. Give a teammate a sliver of space and he will find him. Maxey sits at the center of a loaded Sixers offense still finding its rhythm, and James has added another layer of playmaking to it.The two have history. James first met Maxey at his house before the 2020 draft, when a 19-year-old Maxey spent the visit playing video games with Bronny and Bryce. James has said Maxey is the same person now as he was then, respectful to everyone in the house and down to earth. They also trained together over several offseasons, and James has praised the guard’s work ethic.When James told the Lakers he was leaving, Maxey was among the first to call. James shared the story on his Mind the Game podcast. The pitch was casual. “We can use you down here,” Maxey told him, in James’ retelling.Philadelphia was not high on James’ list at first, with Cleveland and Miami also in the running. He passed on a homecoming with the Cavaliers and a return to the Heat because he wanted a place to chase a fifth championship. He has said the Jaylen Brown trade changed his view, and that Maxey’s presence mattered too.He “just loves everything” about the guard.The numbers back up the pitch. Through the opening weeks, Maxey is averaging 28 points, fifth in the league, while shooting 48.6 percent. His 11 fourth-quarter points per game lead the NBA, which gives James’ passing a ready target late in games. Last season Maxey set career highs at 28.3 points, 4.1 rebounds and 6.6 assists, and he made his first All-NBA team.
Article Summary: LeBron James and Tyrese Maxey have a long history. Maxey was the first person James called when he told him he was leaving the Lakers. James has praised Maxey's work ethic and playmaking ability. The Philadelphia 76ers guard is averaging 28 points, fifth in the league.

Article Title: Why Scotland suspended cricket ties with Afghanistan outside ICC events
Article Text:
Cricket Scotland said its decision was guided by its commitment to expanding women's and girls' participation in the sport

Why Scotland has taken a stand against Afghanistan cricket

ICC matches allowed, but training facilities denied

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Cricket Scotland has decided to suspend cricketing engagement with Afghanistan outside International Cricket Council (ICC) events, citing the Taliban government's treatment of women and girls and wider human rights concerns.The governing body will continue to play Afghanistan in ICC tournaments but will not proactively schedule bilateral series or participate in tri-series involving the men's side unless there is a material change in the circumstances surrounding women's cricket in the country and broader human rights considerations.The decision was approved by the Cricket Scotland Board at a recent meeting of Cricket Scotland Council Limited (CSCL), following an approach by the Afghanistan Cricket Board (ACB) seeking access to training facilities in Scotland.“Cricket Scotland will not proactively schedule bilateral series or participate in tri-series involving Afghanistan Men unless there is a material change in the circumstances surrounding Afghanistan women's cricket and wider human rights considerations,” the governing body said in its statement.Cricket Scotland said its decision was guided by its strategic commitment to expanding women's and girls' participation in the sport, alongside concerns about the humanitarian situation in Afghanistan.Women's sport has effectively disappeared in the country since the Taliban returned to power in 2021. Women and girls have also faced severe restrictions on education and employment opportunities.One of Cricket Scotland's four strategic priorities is the advancement and growth of women's and girls' cricket. Its board considered the treatment of women and girls, the country's humanitarian situation, its commitment to equality, consultation with the government and the positions taken by other major cricket governing bodies.The move follows similar decisions by Cricket Australia and the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB), which have suspended bilateral cricketing engagement with Afghanistan over concerns about women's rights.The Taliban government maintains that it respects women's rights in accordance with its interpretation of Islamic law and local customs, and that internal matters should be addressed locally.Cricket Scotland has clarified that its policy does not extend to ICC tournaments, where fixtures will be determined by competition regulations.“Cricket Scotland will continue to participate in any fixtures against Afghanistan Men at ICC events which are determined by ICC competition regulations,” its statement said.However, the governing body will not host or participate in pre-tour training camps, practice matches or warm-up fixtures involving Afghanistan outside ICC events.The ACB approached Cricket Scotland in July seeking training facilities ahead of the men's series against Ireland. A second request was made in September in connection with the Afghanistan Premier League (APL). The July request was declined due to operational restrictions and to allow the board to consider its position.On franchise cricket, Cricket Scotland said it would honour its contractual obligations to players and issue no-objection certificates (NOCs) if the ICC grants the Afghan league official approval.“If an NOC is issued, participation by that player/s must not be interpreted as an endorsement by Cricket Scotland of the current Afghan regime or its policies,” the statement said.The policy will be reviewed annually or following any significant ICC decision or material change in circumstances.
Article Summary: Cricket Scotland has decided to suspend cricketing engagement with Afghanistan outside International Cricket Council (ICC) events. The governing body will continue to play Afghanistan in ICC tournaments but will not proactively schedule bilateral series or participate in tri-series involving the men's side. Women's sport has effectively disappeared in the country since the Taliban returned to power in 2021.

Article Title: ‘Australian fans have not moved on’: Michael Clarke joins Sandpapergate storm as pressure mounts on Cricket Australia
Article Text:
Usman Khawaja and David Warner. (Getty Images)

Clarke wants the complete truth to emerge

Starc stands by bowlers as Warner backs Khawaja

Cricket Australia refuses to reopen investigation

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

The controversy surrounding Australia's 2018 Sandpapergate scandal has taken another turn, with former captain Michael Clarke joining the growing chorus demanding that Cricket Australia (CA) reopen its investigation following Usman Khawaja 's explosive revelations.Clarke believes Australian cricket fans have still not received the complete truth about the ball-tampering episode and said the issue would continue to haunt the game until the investigation was revisited. His comments come amid contrasting accounts from former teammates, with David Warner backing Khawaja's version, Mitchell Starc standing by the bowlers' earlier statement and CA chief executive Todd Greenberg ruling out another probe.“We haven’t moved on. Australian fans have not moved on. They can’t trust what’s real. They don’t know the truth – until this (investigation) gets reopened and the truth comes out,” Clarke said on 2DayFM’s Breakfast with Nath & Emma.Khawaja reignited the debate through his forthcoming autobiography, Sabr, claiming that the entire Australian Test dressing room, including players and support staff, knew about the use of sandpaper during the 2018 tour of South Africa.The controversy first erupted during the third Test at Cape Town, where Cameron Bancroft was caught on camera attempting to alter the condition of the ball. Smith, Warner and Bancroft subsequently received suspensions, with the latter two also facing additional sanctions.Clarke said the opportunity to establish the complete truth had been missed in 2018 and again when Bancroft made comments about the involvement of other players in a 2021 interview with The Guardian.“We had the chance in 2018. The truth didn’t come out. We had the chance in 2021 when (Cameron Bancroft) made those comments (to The Guardian). The truth didn’t come out. Now we’ve got this opportunity. I would just like to see whatever the truth is for it all to come out, allow people to finally tell the truth, and move on,” he said.Clarke also raised questions about whether the alleged ball-tampering had started before the Cape Town Test, as claimed by Khawaja.“For me, right now, there’s more questions than answers. I want to know, firstly, did everyone know? Because certain players have come out and said they didn’t. I want to know: did they know or not? That’s important information so we can get the truth. And did it happen in the game before? That’s also what I’m hearing, that (it didn’t just happen) in Cape Town,” Clarke added.The latest developments have exposed sharply contrasting positions among members of the Australian side involved in the scandal.Warner, who received a 12-month ban for his role in the episode, publicly backed Khawaja, describing his account as “100% accurate”. He also criticised CA's original investigation as “botched” and “rushed”.“I haven’t really paid much attention to be fair, obviously there’s differing opinions of eight years ago,” Starc told reporters in Sydney.“We were heavily drilled through the process at the time, and since and I guess I won’t speak on behalf of the bowlers, but where I stand, my opinion hasn’t changed. My recollection hasn’t changed from what we said in 2021.”The statement had been issued by Starc, Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon after Bancroft's 2021 interview raised questions about how much the bowling group knew. The quartet denied knowing that a foreign substance had been taken onto the field to alter the ball.Starc also said Khawaja's claim that sandpaper had been used during the second Test in Gqeberha was news to him.“I'll leave said authors to explain,” he said.Despite the renewed calls for answers, Greenberg has ruled out reopening the investigation, saying CA remains satisfied with the original findings.“There are specific details in his book that contradict the versions that have been provided by others,” Greenberg said.“But we have said we’re comfortable with the outcome of the investigation based on the information we’ve received.”He added: “That includes what we’ve seen from Usman, and our position hasn’t changed on that.”Meanwhile, Khawaja responded on social media to suggestions that his revelations were intended to boost sales of his autobiography.“I'm very fortunate, I don't need the money,” he said.With Clarke now joining Warner in questioning the original investigation, and Starc maintaining the bowlers' position, the Sandpapergate controversy continues to divide Australian cricket nearly eight years after the incident.
Article Summary: Michael Clarke calls for Cricket Australia to reopen investigation. Former captain says Australian cricket fans have not received the complete truth about the ball-tampering episode. David Warner backs Usman Khawaja's version of events. Mitchell Starc stands by the bowlers' earlier statement. Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg rules out reopening investigation.

Article Title: Aaryavir Sehwag joins Shubman Gill, Mayank Agarwal in elite list with stunning 160 against UAE
Article Text:
Aaryavir Sehwag

Sehwag falls short of Rayudu's long-standing record

From cautious start to a boundary-filled assault

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Aaryavir Sehwag produced a sensational innings of 160 to join India captain Shubman Gill and Mayank Agarwal in an elite list of Indian batters during the ACC U19 Asia Cup clash against the United Arab Emirates at the Al Amerat Cricket Ground in Oman on Tuesday.The right-hander struck 17 fours and seven sixes in his 168-ball knock, registering the joint fifth-highest individual score by an Indian batter in Youth ODIs. His effort also matched the 160s scored by Gill and Agarwal at the Under-19 level.Gill had scored 160 against England at Mumbai's Wankhede Stadium in 2017, while Agarwal reached the same score against Australia in Hobart in 2009.Sehwag, son of former India opener Virender Sehwag, also shared a massive 193-run partnership for the second wicket with VK Vineeth, putting India in a commanding position after UAE won the toss and elected to field.Sehwag looked set to challenge the long-standing record for the highest individual score by an Indian in Youth ODIs, but his marathon innings came to an end in the 45th over.He was dismissed for 160 off 168 balls, caught by Uddish Suri at mid-wicket off Naseem Khan in the 45th over. Attempting to pull a slower short-of-length delivery across the line, Sehwag failed to get the required timing and found the fielder.The record remains with Ambati Rayudu, who scored an unbeaten 177 against England U19 in Taunton in 2002.Vaibhav Sooryavanshi came close to breaking that mark earlier in 2026, smashing 175 off just 80 balls against England in the Under-19 World Cup final. Sooryavanshi also occupies the third position on the list with his 171 against UAE in 2025.Raj Bawa's unbeaten 162 against Uganda in 2022 is the fourth-highest score by an Indian in Youth ODIs.Sehwag's 160 puts him alongside Gill and Agarwal in the next position on the list.Sehwag began his innings cautiously as India reached 42 without loss in the first 10 overs. However, once settled, he shifted gears and took on the UAE bowling attack, combining boundaries with smart running between the wickets.His partnership with Vineeth proved crucial in rebuilding and accelerating India's innings after the opening stand. The 193-run second-wicket association gave India the platform to push for a substantial total.India had entered the contest looking to bounce back after their three-wicket defeat to Pakistan in their previous group match. Despite Arjun Rajput's century, India were bowled out for 208 before Pakistan chased down the target, powered by Hamza Zahoor's match-winning hundred.
Article Summary: Aaryavir Sehwag scores 160 to join Shubman Gill and Mayank Agarwal in elite list of Indian batters. The right-hander struck 17 fours and seven sixes in his 168-ball knock. He also shared a 193-run partnership for the second wicket with VK Vineeth. His innings came to an end in the 45th over.

Article Title: Lindsay Clancy case: Judge rejects bid to dismiss murder charges, paving way for possible retrial
Article Text:
Lindsay Clancy/Image: Reuters

A Massachusetts judge has rejected Lindsay Clancy's request to dismiss the murder charges against her, ruling that a second trial over the deaths of her three children would not violate her constitutional protection against double jeopardy.Judge William Sullivan ruled on Monday that there was sufficient legal justification for declaring her first trial a mistrial in September. He also rejected a prosecution request for a gag order restricting public statements by the parties involved in the case.The ruling follows arguments presented last week by Clancy's defence team, which maintained that holding another trial would amount to double jeopardy. Her lawyers argued that the judge had not exhausted all available options to resolve a disagreement among jurors before ending the first trial.Sullivan disagreed, concluding that there was a legal basis for the mistrial under the principle of “manifest necessity”. The standard requires that all reasonable options for reaching a verdict be exhausted before a trial can be terminated.In his ruling, the judge also rejected claims that the juror responsible for the deadlock had refused to participate in deliberations.“The foreperson's notes did not plausibly suggest that Juror Doe refused to consider the trial evidence or disagreed with the law as explained by the Court in its instructions,” Sullivan wrote as cited by CNN.He added that information about the juror that emerged after the trial could not be used to challenge the decision to declare a mistrial.The defence had sought access to records relating to the juror, including his phone records and jury selection questionnaire. Sullivan denied the request, saying the material was not relevant to the motion to dismiss or any potential retrial. He also found no grounds to require the juror to testify under oath.The juror, identified as Michael Péguy Desronvil, had faced public scrutiny after the first trial ended. He subsequently said that accounts given by some fellow jurors to the media had misrepresented his position.Sullivan also indicated that he was considering March 2027 for the next trial, with the parties expected to return to court next Monday to discuss scheduling.However, the Plymouth County District Attorney's Office has not formally confirmed whether it intends to prosecute Clancy again. Prosecutors remained noncommittal during last week's hearing and declined to comment on Monday's developments.Clancy's defence attorney, Kevin Reddington, had questioned the prosecution's delay in deciding whether to pursue another trial and what charges his client might face.In a separate ruling, Sullivan rejected prosecutors' request for restrictions on statements made by Clancy's legal team outside court. He said the prosecution had not demonstrated that those comments posed a serious risk of prejudicing jury selection or the outcome of a future trial.The judge said prosecutors could renew their request if circumstances changed, while reminding the defence team of its professional obligations.
Article Summary: A Massachusetts judge has rejected Lindsay Clancy's request to dismiss the murder charges against her. Judge William Sullivan ruled that there was sufficient legal justification for declaring her first trial a mistrial in September. He also rejected a prosecution request for a gag order restricting public statements by the parties involved in the case.

Article Title: Skydance Games cuts jobs a month after Warner Bros merger; company says: This is not a reflection of...
Article Text:
Warner Bros merger brings first job cuts at Skydance Games

Skydance Interactive and Paramount Games staff bear the brunt of the layoffs

Skydance has promised Wall Street at least $6 billion in merger savings

Skydance Games has cut jobs barely a month after its parent company closed its $110 billion takeover of Warner Bros. Discovery. The gaming division is among the first parts of the newly merged entertainment giant to be trimmed, with developers across art, design, engineering and writing affected over the last few days.A Skydance spokesperson said the company had stepped back to rethink where it invests its efforts and decided to scale down some of its projects. "As a result, there are roles impacted," the spokesperson said, adding that the cuts did not reflect the talent or creativity of those leaving. The company hasn't shared how many jobs were lost or which projects are being pared back, though reports put the number at 30 or more.The cuts appear to have landed on staff who came from Skydance Interactive, the studio behind The Walking Dead: Saints & Sinners, and Paramount Games. Warner Bros. Games employees do not seem to be part of this round.Rebecca Vessal, a senior gameplay and game AI programmer who kept her job, wrote on LinkedIn that "most of my game team at Skydance Interactive got laid off today." Engineer David Vera, also unaffected, posted that Skydance "just lost a ton of great talent yesterday" and stressed that nobody was let go over performance, before sharing a long list of former colleagues open to new roles.Skydance and Paramount merged their gaming businesses in the summer to form Paramount Games Studio, whose slate includes Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: The Last Ronin and Avatar Legends: The Fighting Game. Once the Warner deal closed on October 6, it was combined with Warner's in-house developers, including Avalanche Software, NetherRealm, Rocksteady and TT Games, under the Skydance Games banner. Tony Driscoll, who previously oversaw Fortnite's creator economy at Epic Games, heads the group as president of games and experiences.The layoffs coincide with co-CEOs David Ellison and Ynon Kreiz presenting their first quarterly results since the deal on Monday. The pair have committed to at least $6 billion in cost synergies and have said layoffs will be part of that. Late in October, the company also brought in a five-day office mandate and a voluntary buyout programme.Gaming has barely featured in the merger conversation. When leadership has brought it up, the focus has been on big names, with Ellison and Kreiz pointing to Hogwarts Legacy and Mortal Kombat in an October memo, and Driscoll highlighting Batman.The wider industry isn't offering much cushion either. Microsoft offered voluntary buyouts to a quarter of its workforce last month, Xbox staff included. For the developers Skydance has let go, that makes for a crowded job market to walk into.
Article Summary: Warner Bros merger brings first job cuts at Skydance Games. Game developers across art, design, engineering and writing affected. Spokesperson says the cuts did not reflect the talent or creativity of those leaving. The company hasn't shared how many jobs were lost or which projects are being pared back.

Article Title: Fresh Sandpapergate storm puts Mitchell Starc in spotlight; Alyssa Healy reveals her stance: 'Slightly conflicted'
Article Text:
Alyssa Healy (Photo/Getty Images)

Alyssa Healy reacts to fresh Sandpapergate allegations involving Mitchell Starc

What is the Sandpapergate controversy?

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

Healy urges empathy for those involved in Sandpapergate

The infamous Sandpapergate scandal has returned to haunt Australian cricket, with fresh claims from former batter Usman Khawaja reigniting debate over the 2018 ball-tampering controversy. This time, the spotlight has fallen on Mitchell Starc, with his wife and former Australia women's captain Alyssa Healy admitting that she feels "slightly conflicted" about the renewed allegations.Khawaja, in his newly released autobiography Sabr, made explosive revelations about the 2018 Cape Town Test against South Africa, claiming that the entire Australian Test team was aware of the use of sandpaper to tamper with the ball. He also alleged that ball-tampering was not restricted to the infamous third Test, with the practice reportedly taking place during the second Test of the series as well.Starc, however, has firmly rejected Khawaja's claims, maintaining that he stands by the joint statement released in 2021 alongside Pat Cummins, Josh Hazlewood and Nathan Lyon. The four Australian fast bowlers had denied knowing about the sandpaper being taken onto the field and the ball being tampered with during the Cape Town Test.Speaking at Kayo Sports and Fox Cricket's launch event, Healy admitted that the situation was difficult for her to comment on, given her personal connection to the controversy."It's a hard one to comment on. At the moment, I feel slightly conflicted, and I'm in the middle of it. It's hard to make a comment on it, we'll see where it goes and if CA do take it forward or how it rolls throughout the media, and I'll make a comment from there. For now, I'm just gonna sit and wait and watch it unfold," Healy said.Her comments come after Starc publicly pushed back against Khawaja's version of events, insisting that his position on the controversy remains unchanged.The Sandpapergate scandal dates back to the third Test between Australia and South Africa at Newlands, Cape Town, in March 2018. During the match, television cameras captured Cameron Bancroft using a piece of sandpaper to alter the condition of the ball.The incident triggered one of the biggest controversies in Australian cricket history. Bancroft was handed a nine-month suspension, while then-captain Steve Smith and vice-captain David Warner received 12-month bans from international and domestic cricket. Smith was also removed from the captaincy, while Warner was banned from holding a leadership position in Australian cricket.Khawaja's latest revelations have brought the episode back into the spotlight, with questions being raised about how widespread the knowledge of the ball-tampering operation was within the Australian dressing room.However, Cricket Australia chief executive Todd Greenberg has indicated that the governing body has little interest in reopening the matter more than eight years after the incident. Healy backed that approach, suggesting that Australian cricket should focus on moving forward rather than revisiting a controversy that had already left a lasting impact on those involved."I watched it eight years ago too. I think the game of cricket as a whole has moved on. (Cricket Australia CEO) Todd Greenberg's statement today about not looking into it any further is a great sign of where we're headed and that's moving forward and looking ahead to this summer," she said.She said the individuals mentioned in Khawaja's book were being forced to revisit difficult memories and urged people to consider the emotional toll of the renewed scrutiny."I feel for everyone involved. I know a human element in it as well that people are being dragged back through some things and reliving some memories. I think from a human side of things we've got to remember that and put our arms around the people that are being mentioned," she added.
Article Summary: Alyssa Healy reacts to fresh Sandpapergate allegations involving Mitchell Starc. Former Australia women's captain says she feels "slightly conflicted" about the renewed allegations. Comes after fresh claims from former batter Usman Khawaja reignited debate over the 2018 ball-tampering controversy.

Article Title: Fujifilm Instax Mini Evo Cinema review: It’s hard not to want one
Article Text:
Instax, all the way up

It is a joy to pick up and play with

The footage is made for the moment

Evo Cinema's charm lives in the little rituals

Our rating: 3.5/5

Nostalgia sells, and few companies understand that better than Fujifilm. Instax is proof enough. Phones should have made a camera that prints small, slightly imperfect photos irrelevant a long time ago, yet Instax has only kept growing, largely among people who care less about how a picture looks and more about having one to hold. The Instax Mini Evo Cinema takes everything that has made Instax work and turns it all the way up.It is a video camera, a stills camera and an Instax printer squeezed into a body modelled on Fujifilm's sixties-era Fujica Single-8, with a dial on the side that rolls the clock back through ten decades of film and video. Wanting one takes about a minute. Working out whether you really need one takes a little longer.Nothing about the Evo Cinema is held the way a camera usually is. It stands upright like an old cine camera, three fingers curled around a stubby grip and the index finger resting on a trigger tucked under the lens. Squeeze, and it records. Let go, or hit 15 seconds, and it stops. At 270g, in dark grey with small green accents, it looks far more grown-up than the pastel Instax cameras most people know. Fujifilm also puts two small accessories in the box that make a real difference: a grip extension that screws into the tripod socket and gives the little finger somewhere to rest, and a magnetic eyepiece that clips over the rear screen.Snap the eyepiece on, raise the camera to your eye, and for a moment it feels less like a new gadget and more like something that lived in a cupboard at your grandparents' place.People notice it, and they want to hold it before they even ask what it does. That rarely happens with a new phone.The dial on the left is where the evening disappears. Turn it to the thirties and the little screen flickers into black and white, with scratches drifting across the frame. The fifties look like an early television broadcast, and the sixties wash the colours out as sprocket holes creep in along the edges. The eighties stamp an orange date in the corner, just like the prints from the neighbourhood photo studio, while the nineties bring back the wobbly, slightly smeared look of a tape camcorder. The 2000s borrow the blocky on-screen icons of an early digicam, and the 2010s go as far as a livestream-style overlay. Even the audio plays along, muffling voices and adding the whirr of a film reel in the older decades, and in a few of them, a quick shake of the camera throws in glitches from that era. A ring around the lens dials each look up or down across ten levels, which makes for a hundred variations, and a small switch adds frames to suit the decade.So everything gets filmed. A desk. A street corner. A cup of chai in faded 1940s colour, then a friend laughing through a nineties haze, each clip in a different decade simply because turning the dial is that much fun.Printing comes with its own little ritual. There is no button; a lever folds out of the side and needs a firm quarter twist, much like winding film through a cine camera, before an Instax Mini print slides out of the top. It serves no practical purpose and it is satisfying every single time.Freeze a clip, print a frame, and the camera can add a QR code in the corner that plays the full video for anyone who scans it. The clip is uploaded through the Instax app and stays on Fujifilm's servers for two years, and the same app can stitch a few clips into a 30-second short with a title card up front. Pass one of those prints across the table at a house party and watch the phones come out.On the Evo Cinema's own 1.54-inch screen, every clip looks wonderful, and that screen is small enough to be generous. Play the same clips on a phone and they turn noticeably softer, which is what 600x800 pixels from a 1/5-inch sensor will do. The older decades carry it off with ease, since grain and blur are part of their charm anyway. The cleaner settings from 2000 onwards are a little less forgiving, and 2020, with no effect at all, is the most honest of the lot. That last one does get a higher-quality 1080x1440 mode, though it only works with a microSD card inside and has to be switched on from the menu.Because the camera is built to be held upright, video comes out in a tall 3:4 frame. Turn it sideways for a wider shot and the TV-style scan lines of the older decades turn sideways with it. The zoom is digital too, and it moves in small steps that show up if you use it mid-clip.It has a few other habits worth knowing about. Waking up takes a few seconds, and so does every turn of the dial, so hopping between decades comes with a short pause each time. Every clip ends with a keep-or-discard prompt that is easy to skip past in the rush to the next shot. The decade you pick stays baked in for good, the small built-in microphone is fine for voices up close and not much further, and the internal battery prefers short outings; an evening of shooting followed by transfers to the phone is usually enough to run it down.None of it takes much away while you are out with the camera. These clips are at their best right then, passed around on that tiny screen while everyone is still laughing.Once the first rush settles, it gets easier to see where the Evo Cinema's charm really comes from. Set the dial and the lever aside for a moment, and a large part of it rests on the filters. They are some of the most thoughtful Fujifilm has made, and a real dial beats a slider on a screen every time. Phones, though, have offered VHS, Super 8 and film grain looks through editing apps for years, along with sharper video, no clip limit and an untouched original to fall back on. Once posted, both clips sit side by side in the same Instagram story.That is probably why, after the first day, the Evo Cinema slowly made its way from the bag to the desk and eventually into a drawer. Nothing went wrong with it; the phone was simply already in hand, and happy to do most of the same work.Printing is the one thing that keeps pulling it back out, and it is also where the Evo Cinema quietly does its best work. The app sends photos from your phone straight to the built-in printer, and since a phone captures far more detail than the camera's own 5-megapixel sensor, those prints often look better than the ones shot on the Evo Cinema itself. The QR code is a delightful idea as well. Even so, Fujifilm's standalone Instax printers cover much of the same ground for less.Then there is the price. Fujifilm has set the Mini Evo Cinema at Rs 47,999 before a single pack of film, the most it has ever asked for an Instax camera, and about what a well-kept older iPhone sells for these days. Still photos and printing from a phone are part of the deal, and they help, just not quite enough to close that gap.None of that takes away from what Fujifilm has built. The Evo Cinema is thoughtfully designed, more charming than almost anything else on the shelf, and nearly impossible to hand over without getting a smile back. Most of that magic, though, lands on day one, in the trigger, the lever, the dial and the first print sliding out. For anyone who grew up loving Instax prints and has something set aside for a purely joyful purchase, it will bring a lot of happiness.For most others, the phone in their pocket has been doing much of this for years, just with a little less ceremony.
Article Summary: The Instax Mini Evo Cinema takes everything that has made Instax work and turns it all the way up. It is a video camera, a stills camera and an Instax printer squeezed into a body modelled on Fujifilm's sixties-era Fujica Single-8. The dial on the side rolls the clock back through ten decades of film and video.

Article Title: Delhi's worst had PM2.5 at 83x of standard. Oh, wait, Jahangirpuri tops Diwali hall of shame. And, then, it doesn’t
Article Text:
During Diwali, PM2.5 levels in Delhi reached alarming heights, particularly in Jahangirpuri and Mundka (Representative image)

PM2.5 over 330 times WHO limit





NEW DELHI: The hourly PM2.5 concentration at northwest Delhi’s Jahangirpuri spiked to 4,985 micrograms per cubic metre (µg/m³) at 6pm and 8pm on Diwali, before shooting up again at 8am the next day, making it the most polluted location Sunday and Monday in the city.This was around 83 times the daily national ambient air quality standard of 60 µg/m³ and over 332 times World Health Organisation’s (WHO) daily safe guideline of 15 µg/m³.However, Delhi Pollution Control Committee (DPCC) changed the readings Monday night, showing that Jahangirpuri hit its peak PM2.5 levels at 776 µg/m³ at Diwali midnight.The pattern of extreme pollution around midnight was witnessed in most parts of the city when firecrackers were set off in large numbers.A TOI analysis of DPCC real-time air quality data shows that most stations witnessed a sharp rise in PM2.5 levels around midnight. Thereafter, the pollution levels remained high till at least 6am Monday.At Mundka, the hourly PM2.5 levels jumped from 245 µg/m³ at 7pm on Diwali to 3,744 µg/m³ at 2am Monday.A similar trend was witnessed across the city. JNU saw a peak hourly PM2.5 concentration of 3,023 µg/m³ at 4am Monday; it was just 118 µg/m³ at 7pm Sunday.The peak reading at NSUT (west campus) was 3,008 µg/m³ and 2,908 µg/m³ at Mandir Marg.The stations, which recorded hazardous levels of hourly PM2.5 levels, included Nehru Nagar in Lajpat Nagar (2,808 µg/m³), Wazirpur (2,721), Talkatora Garden (2,599), CWG Sports Complex in Akshardham (2,471), Patparganj (2,597) and Ashok Vihar (2,589).Sunil Dahiya, founder of Envirocatalyst, a think tank, said, “Through Diwali night, people across Delhi inhaled PM2.5 averaging 450 to 550 µg/m³. That is eight to nine times the national 24-hour standard and 30 to 37 times WHO’s guideline. Even a few hours at these levels can trigger asthma attacks, worsen lung diseases and raise the risk of heart attacks and strokes.”Dahiya said children, the elderly, pregnant women, outdoor workers and people with heart or lung conditions are hit hardest in such situations.“Fine particles reach deep into their lungs and bloodstream, and the coarser PM10 inflames airways and eyes. One night was added to a season in which Delhi’s air was already more than twice the safe limit before a single cracker was burst,” he said.Several locations in Delhi recorded high hourly PM10 levels.It reached 4,697 µg/m³ at Punjabi Bagh, making it nearly 47 times higher than the daily national ambient air quality standard for PM10 at 100 µg/m³. It was more than 104 times higher than WHO’s daily safe guideline of 45 µg/m³.Hourly PM10 concentrations surged to 3,490 µg/m³ at Anand Vihar, 3,929 at Patparganj, 2,881 at RK Puram, 2,879 at Nehru Nagar and 2,671 at Wazirpur.
Article Summary: PM2.5 levels in Delhi reached alarming heights, particularly in Jahangirpuri and Mundka. The pattern of extreme pollution around midnight was witnessed in most parts of the city when firecrackers were set off in large numbers. The pollution levels remained high till at least 6am Monday.

Article Title: X locks TOI photojournalist Anindya Chattopadhyay's account after smog posts
Article Text:
Anindya Chattopadhyay,found himself at the center of a storm when his X account faced a lock due to smog images

X post

I was only doing my duty, X locked my account





NEW DELHI: TOI photographer Anindya Chattopadhyay's X account was locked after he posted photos & videos showing "deadly smog" and poor visibility around NH9 and Lodhi Garden, with the platform citing a "violation of its rules".Chattopadhyay said it was his duty to show "the truth of the post-Diwali situation through my camera".As Delhi woke up to a thick blanket of post-Diwali smog Monday, I found myself at the centre of an unexpected controversy.My X account was locked after I posted photographs and videos showing poor visibility around NH9 and Lodhi Garden, with the platform citing a “violation of its rules”.I left home at 6.30am and headed towards Akshardham. Near NH9, visibility dropped so sharply that I had to park my scooter on the side of the highway.Standing on a footoverbridge, I began filming the haze. After waiting 15-20 minutes for visibility to improve slightly, I resumed my journey towards Lodhi Garden.The scene there was no better. The city's iconic tombs were barely visible through the dense smog. Concerned by the conditions, I started uploading the photographs and videos to my X account.Delhi govt, however, denied any involvement in the locking of the account.
Article Summary: TOI photographer Anindya Chattopadhyay's X account was locked after he posted photos & videos showing "deadly smog" and poor visibility around NH9 and Lodhi Garden. The platform cited a "violation of its rules", but Delhi govt denied any involvement in the locking.

Article Title: GTA 6: The Festival brings Travis Scott, Cardi B and more to Miami for a massive launch celebration
Article Text:
(Courtesy : Rockstar Games)

GTA 6: The Festival announces Travis Scott, Cardi B and Cardi B's fellow stars

GTA 6: The Festival tickets, lottery rules and registration details

Grand Theft Auto 6 is preparing to make noise beyond the gaming world. Rockstar Games has added a major musical attraction to the highly anticipated release, bringing some of the biggest names in hip-hop, electronic and Latin music together for a one-night festival in Miami. Travis Scott Cardi B and Don Toliver are among the headline performers. The event will give fans another reason to celebrate the arrival of GTA 6, turning its launch week into a much bigger cultural moment. However, getting inside the venue may prove just as exciting as the performances themselves.Rockstar Games has confirmed that The Festival will take place on November 21, 2026, at Mana Wynwood in Miami. The concert will follow the official release of GTA 6 on November 19, giving fans two days to explore the new game before the celebrations begin.The musical lineup brings together artists from different corners of the industry. Travis Scott will appear through Cactus Jack Presents, alongside Don Toliver, Kodak Black and SoFaygo. Cardi B also joins the bill, adding another major name to an already impressive list.The remaining performers include Ca7riel and Paco Amoroso, Justice with a DJ set, Metro Boomin, Nick León B2B DJ Python, Prospa B2B Skream, Rauw and Friends, Suero, Tainy, and The Dare B2B Fcukers.The mix of performers reflects the musical identity Rockstar wants to bring to GTA 6. Hip-hop, Latin sounds, electronic music and dance tracks will all have a place at the event. For fans, this is also an opportunity to experience music associated with the game outside the virtual world.The concert could become one of the biggest promotional events surrounding the release, especially with several internationally recognised performers sharing the same stage.While the lineup has already generated excitement, fans will need to secure access through Rockstar Games' lottery-based ticket system. Rather than offering unrestricted public sales, the company is using a random selection process to determine who gets an opportunity to purchase tickets.Participants must be at least 17 years old, and each person can submit only one entry. Rockstar will randomly select successful applicants and send them a presale code through SMS.Receiving a code does not mean unlimited access. Each successful entry will allow the selected person to purchase a maximum of two tickets.This system could make the event particularly competitive, given the popularity of the performers and the enormous interest surrounding GTA 6.The Festival also gives Rockstar a chance to connect the game's soundtrack with real-world music culture. With Travis Scott, Cardi B, Metro Boomin and several other major performers involved, the Miami celebration is shaping up to be a major highlight of GTA 6 launch week.
Article Summary: Travis Scott, Cardi B and Don Toliver are among the headline performers. The Festival will take place on November 21, 2026, at Mana Wynwood in Miami. The concert will follow the official release of GTA 6 on November 19. Rockstar Games is using a lottery-based ticket system.

Article Title: Day after Diwali, Mumbai AQI nearly 20% better than last year; pollution surges in some pockets at night
Article Text: Mumbai: The city’s air was much cleaner overall on Monday after Diwali, with govt and private trackers showing low pollution numbers. However, firecrackers burst late in the night caused sharp spikes in a few areas.Overall, Mumbai logged an official average air quality index (AQI) of 172 for the 24-hour period beginning 4pm on Sunday—an 18.5% improvement compared to last year, when the AQI hit 211 the day after Diwali. While the citywide average stayed out of the severe zone, at least nine locations slipped into the ‘poor’ category, with AQI readings crossing 200.Bandra East was the most polluted area for the second day in a row, with a PM10 level of 194. Although still high, it was a big drop from Sunday, when readings crossed 400.As the night went on, pollution shot up suddenly in select spots. Deonar’s PM10 went from 93 in the evening to 426 at 11pm. Andheri East saw PM2.5 jump from 39 at 8pm to 145 by 11pm. On the other hand, areas like Ghatkopar, Colaba and Byculla saw no major jump at night, ending the festival on a cleaner note.While firecrackers can temporarily drive up local pollution by 50% to 60% for a few hours, experts noted that their overall contribution to the city’s yearly average is tiny—around 1%.“Firecrackers can temporarily dominate local pollution levels, sometimes contributing 50-60% or even more of the particulate pollution during peak hours in severely affected locations. Their impact can last 6-8 hours, depending on meteorological conditions. But, their contribution to annual average pollution is considerably smaller. The exact contribution varies by location, emission inventory and averaging period,” said independent meteorologist Abhijith Modak.Weighing in on how citizens should read extremely high local pollution numbers, Gufran Beig, chair professor at Indian Institute of Advanced Studies, said: “Cracker-induced pollution numbers are bad for 1-2 hours only, giving figures like 600 momentarily. While publishing AQI numbers, rolling 24-hour averages should be captured instead of hourly readings. The 24-hour average helps in understanding if the high numbers are a perennial high or just momentary. ” He said hourly readings “don’t really mean much and they only lead to momentary outrage for 2-3 days and a complete lack of interest thereafter throughout the year”.Beig asked that a regulatory body look into the numbers being put out by private portals. “On the other hand, govt AQI data needs to be more citizen and layman friendly so that common people understand what it represents.”
Article Summary: Mumbai logged an official average air quality index (AQI) of 172 for the 24-hour period beginning 4pm on Sunday. While the citywide average stayed out of the severe zone, at least nine locations slipped into the ‘poor’ category.

Article Title: Suicide abetment: Accused man held, spouse at large
Article Text: Navi Mumbai: After a week of manhunt, the Rasayani police have arrested the accused man wanted for the suicide abetment of a 32-year-old woman and her two kids, who had jumped to their deaths from their 11th-floor apartment in Hiranandani Fortune City complex on the night of Nov 2, after being threatened for recovery of a Rs 2 lakh loan they had given to her husband.The arrested accused has been identified as Vishwanath Desai. His spouse Akshara (29), who is also an accused, is being traced. They reside in Pune and are natives of Solapur. The deceased were identified as Manasi Popete, her son Rudra (11) and daughter Hansika (6). Three days ago, the police had seized the SUV of the accused Vishwanath Desai from Mumbai and had been relentlessly searching for him and his spouse.An FIR was registered against the accused Desai couple for the offence of suicide abetment, house trespass, criminal intimidation, intentional insult with intent to provoke a breach of the peace and joint criminal liability after the deceased woman’s husband Machindra Popete (42), a real estate agent, lodged a police complaint. Popete had alleged that the Desai couple had been threatening him on the phone as he had not repaid a Rs 2 lakh personal loan that he owed them. The complainant provided to the police the mobile voice call recording of threats received from the accused. The accused Desai couple had gone to Popete’s rented apartment in Minarva society in Hiranandani Fortune City complex at Bhokarpada, Panvel taluka on Nov 2 around 8.45 pm, when he was not at home. They had forcibly entered his apartment by compelling his wife Manasi Popete to open the door by kicking and banging on the door and then threatened her in the presence of the kids. Hence, unable to bear the mental stress due to harassment for recovery of the loan, Manasi, along with her two kids, ended their lives, alleged the complainant Machindra Popete.
Article Summary: The arrested accused has been identified as Vishwanath Desai. His spouse Akshara (29), who is also an accused, is being traced. The deceased were identified as Manasi Popete, her son Rudra (11) and daughter Hansika (6)

Article Title: Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar markets buzz late into night on eve of Laxmi Pujan
Article Text:
From Paithan Gate to Tilak Path, Nirala Bazaar, Osmanpura, Gulmandi, City Chowk, Rangar Galli, Garkheda, Jalna Road, and CIDCO-HUDCO, shoppers thronged the streets with their families

Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar





: The city was soaked in Diwali colours on the eve of Laxmi Pujan, with markets buzzing late into the night.From Paithan Gate to Tilak Path, Nirala Bazaar, Osmanpura, Gulmandi, City Chowk, Rangar Galli, Garkheda, Jalna Road, and CIDCO-HUDCO, shoppers thronged the streets with their families. Readymade garment showrooms saw long waiting times, while stalls selling electric lights, decorative items, rangoli colours, puja materials, and festive food did brisk business.“Buying clothes for our two children proved to be a very tough task as every shop was heavily crowded. We did not expect such a huge rush and will ensure we shop well in advance next time,” said Sonali Upadhye, a homemaker.Old Mondha, Jadhavwadi, and local malls witnessed heavy grocery buying for Diwali snacks. Meanwhile, jewellery showrooms and automobile dealerships are gearing up for padwa, which is traditionally considered highly auspicious for buying gold and vehicles.The firecracker markets at Karnapura, Kalagram, TV Centre, Shivajinagar, Cantonment, Waluj, and the taluka town of Gangapur have also turned into major attractions, especially for youngsters eyeing new, viral fireworks.With schools already closed for the Diwali vacations, children were seen having a merry time.“We play a lot during Diwali vacations, burst firecrackers, and eat a lot of sweets. Diwali vacations end all too fast, though,” said Sarvesh Nanajkar, a primary school student.The Diwali festivities began on Thursday with Vasubaras, as families worshipped cows and calves by visiting nearby gaushalas and decorating their courtyards with rangolis. By Friday evening, the festive mood had completely shifted into full celebration mode.
Article Summary: The city was soaked in Diwali colours on the eve of Laxmi Pujan, with markets buzzing late into the night. Firecracker markets at Karnapura, Kalagram, TV Centre, Shivajinagar, Cantonment, Waluj, and the taluka town of Gangapur have also turned into major attractions.

Article Title: Mumbai-bound traffic hit after hatchback catches fire on Vashi Creek bridge
Article Text:
The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine.





NAVI MUMBAI: Vehicular traffic from Navi Mumbai towards Mumbai was disrupted for around 30 minutes after a hatchback caught fire while crossing the Vashi Creek Bridge on Friday at around 7.30pm.The driver escaped unhurt. He immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. However, the fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred.Vashi traffic police alerted the Vashi fire brigade, which reached the spot within 15 minutes. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.Sunil Kadam, senior inspector of the Vashi traffic unit, said the driver was identified as Sumit Bhikaji Kadam.“At around 7.45pm, we received a call from one Rahul, whose full name is not known, informing us that a car had caught fire on the Mumbai-bound lane of the Vashi Creek Bridge,” said AV Sisode, the on-duty fireman at Vashi fire station.“In the meantime, we also received a call from the Vashi traffic police and immediately rushed to the spot with a fire tender. The Mumbai fire brigade team had also reached the spot as there was some confusion over the jurisdiction,” Sisode said.The fire was subsequently extinguished, and the Vashi fire brigade team returned to the station at around 8.30pm.
Article Summary: The driver immediately pulled the car over to the roadside after noticing smoke emanating from the engine. The fire soon engulfed the entire vehicle, leaving it completely charred. The charred vehicle was later towed away by a crane, following which traffic movement returned to normal.
